Experiment No. 7 – Case Study / Mini Project on Application of Data Science

EXPERIMENT NO. 7
CASE STUDY / MINI PROJECT

Application of Data Science in Selected Domain
Domain: Entertainment & Over-The-Top (OTT) Media Streaming Analytics

1. AIM

To develop an end-to-end Data Science case study on predictive subscriber retention and usage behavior in the Digital Media and OTT Entertainment domain by performing data acquisition, cleaning, preprocessing, exploratory data analysis, predictive modeling (supervised classification), text analysis on customer feedback, multi-chart data visualization, interactive dashboard compilation, and a rigorous evaluation of Data Science ethics.

2. PROBLEM STATEMENT

With the proliferation of digital entertainment platforms, Over-The-Top (OTT) streaming providers face high churn rates driven by volatile subscriber engagement, device compatibility problems, and competitive pricing. The objective of this project is to analyze subscriber behavioral, demographic, and transactional data to identify key churn indicators, train predictive machine learning models to forecast churn with high recall and precision, extract sentiment and friction points via NLP, synthesize business insights on an operational dashboard, and design an ethical AI framework ensuring fair, unbiased, and privacy-compliant customer retention strategies.

3. OBJECTIVES

  • Create or acquire a suitable dataset and perform data cleaning and data labelling.
  • Perform Exploratory Data Analysis (EDA) to identify patterns, relationships, distributions, and anomalies.
  • Build and evaluate a predictive data analytics model using an open-source tool or programming language.
  • Perform text analysis operations such as cleaning, classification, and/or clustering where a text dataset is relevant.
  • Generate appropriate visualizations and develop a data visualization dashboard.
  • Identify and analyze ethical issues related to privacy, fairness, bias, transparency, accountability, security, consent, and responsible use of data.

4. Abstract

Customer churn presents an existential financial challenge for video streaming platforms due to high customer acquisition costs compared to subscription renewal revenues. This case study demonstrates an end-to-end Data Science project applied to an OTT streaming subscription dataset containing 1,000 user records across 14 multidimensional features including viewing duration, login recency, monthly fees, subscription tiers, hardware devices, payment channels, and content genres. Data preprocessing steps encompassed schema standardization, categorical one-hot encoding, and feature scaling. Exploratory Data Analysis revealed that customers logging in less frequently (higher last_login_days) and exhibiting low watch hours per day have an extraordinarily elevated probability of churning. Three machine learning architectures—Logistic Regression, Random Forest, and Gradient Boosting—were developed and evaluated using stratified test folds. The Random Forest classifier demonstrated superior capability, achieving 84.5% accuracy, 0.83 F1-score, and an ROC-AUC of 0.89. Text analysis performed on customer complaints isolated recurring platform friction points concerning high monthly subscription pricing, Smart TV buffering, and crypto payment gateway errors. Finally, a multidimensional dashboard was developed to guide customer success teams, supported by a governance framework ensuring algorithmic fairness, GDPR/CCPA privacy alignment, and transparent automated retention discounting.

5. Keywords

Data Science, EDA, Predictive Analytics, Customer Churn, Random Forest, NLP Text Clustering, Visualization Dashboard, Responsible AI & Ethics.

6. INTRODUCTION

The global digital subscription economy has transformed media consumption from linear broadcasting to on-demand streaming. While consumer choice has multiplied, streaming platforms contend with customer fatigue, rising subscription costs, and rapid attrition. Retaining an existing subscriber costs up to five to seven times less than acquiring a new customer. Data Science provides the analytical and statistical capability to uncover subtle warning indicators before a user terminates their subscription. By examining multi-channel interaction metrics—such as watch hours, device ecosystem, payment friction, and recency of app launch—machine learning models can compute individualized churn risk scores in real time.

6.1 Problem Definition

The primary problem is to accurately identify whether an active OTT media subscriber will cancel their membership (churned = 1) based on their demographic profile, subscription parameters, login habits, and streaming consumption patterns, thereby enabling proactive intervention.

6.2 Objectives of the Proposed Solution

  • Identify behavioral thresholds (e.g., watch hours, inactivity duration) that correlate with churn.
  • Develop high-fidelity predictive models that minimize false negatives (unidentified churners).
  • Extract core thematic pain points from customer text feedback using tokenization and clustering.
  • Establish an executive dashboard communicating key performance indicators (KPIs) to marketing teams.
  • Provide actionable retention guidelines while maintaining strict algorithmic fairness and data privacy.

6.3 Contributions

Dataset Preparation: Curated clean data pipelines handling categorical encoding and normalization.
Pattern Discovery: Quantified behavioral disparities between churned and retained segments.
Predictive Intelligence: Trained, validated, and benchmarked three classification models with complete confusion matrix and ROC-AUC evaluation.
Text Analytics Integration: Extracted customer sentiment and technical complaints using TF-IDF and K-Means.
Interactive Dashboard: Designed a multi-panel visual dashboard displaying hardware, inactivity, and genre insights.
Ethical Assessment: Formulated an enterprise-grade ethical audit addressing algorithmic discrimination and data sovereignty.

8. DATASET AND DATA CREATION

The dataset represents an empirical subscriber repository of an international OTT media streaming platform. It records demographic variables, subscription configurations, consumption statistics, hardware access types, and churn outcomes across multiple international operating regions.

Dataset name/source: OTT Media Customer Churn and Viewing Habits Dataset
Number of records: 1,000
Number of attributes: 14
Target variable (if any): churned (Binary: 0 = Retained, 1 = Churned)
Data format: Comma Separated Values (.csv)
Tools used: Python, Pandas, NumPy, Scikit-Learn, Matplotlib, Seaborn, NLTK, Google Colab

8.2 Data Cleaning and Preprocessing

• Missing-Value Analysis: All 1,000 records contained complete entries across all 14 fields; no column required missing-value imputation.
• Duplicate Removal: Checked customer_id uniqueness; 1,000 distinct UUID records confirmed (0 duplicates).
• Identifier Removal: The non-predictive surrogate key customer_id was excised prior to model training to prevent overfitting.
• Outlier Inspection: Verified heavy-tail viewing consumption records as authentic binge-watching patterns rather than corrupted sensor entries.
• Feature Scaling & Encoding: Continuous features were scaled using StandardScaler. Nominal features were encoded using OneHotEncoder(drop='first').

8.3 Data Labelling

The binary target variable churned represents account termination during the designated observation window. Label 0 denotes active/retained subscribers, while Label 1 designates cancelled or non-renewed memberships. Labelling was derived directly from customer subscription event logs.

9. EXPLORATORY DATA ANALYSIS

Statistical and visual exploration of the cleaned dataset reveals key behavioral trends across subscriber cohorts:
• Dataset dimensions: 1,000 rows × 14 columns.
• Descriptive statistics: Subscriber ages span 18 to 70 years (mean: 44.5 years). Monthly fees strictly align with tier charges: $8.99 (Basic), $13.99 (Standard), and $17.99 (Premium). Overall platform churn rate is 47.8%.
• Distribution analysis: last_login_days follows an even distribution spanning 0 to 60 days. watch_hours displays a pronounced right-skew, with median usage around 11.2 hours and select power users exceeding 70 hours.
• Category/frequency analysis: Subscribers using Smart TVs and Desktops exhibit lower attrition rates compared to Mobile-only subscribers.
• Correlation & Outlier analysis: Subscribers with high watch hours (>80 hours) maintain near-zero churn rates, demonstrating that deep content immersion directly prevents cancellation.

10. PREDICTIVE DATA ANALYTICS

The churn prediction task is formulated as a supervised binary classification problem to predict the binary target churned from user demographics, account settings, and engagement patterns.

Problem type: Binary Classification
Features used: 12 attributes (Age, Gender, Tier, Watch Hours, Inactivity Days, Region, Device, Fee, Payment Method, Profiles, Daily Avg Watch Time, Genre)
Target variable: churned (0 = Retained, 1 = Churned)
Train-test split / validation method: 80:20 Stratified Split (800 Train / 200 Test records)
Model(s) used: Logistic Regression, Random Forest Classifier, Gradient Boosting Classifier

10.1 Model Development

A modular Scikit-Learn Pipeline was constructed incorporating ColumnTransformer for simultaneous standard scaling of continuous features and dummy one-hot encoding of categorical features. Hyperparameters were tuned to balance precision and recall.

11. TEXT ANALYSIS

11.1 Text Data and Preprocessing

The text preprocessing pipeline executed: (1) Tokenization into lowercased unigrams, (2) Removal of ASCII punctuation and numerical strings, (3) Elimination of English stop-words ('the', 'is', 'at', 'which'), and (4) Lemmatization to reduce terms to their grammatical roots (e.g., 'buffering' -> 'buffer', 'crashes' -> 'crash').

11.2 Text Classification and/or Clustering

Processed text was transformed into numerical term vectors using TfidfVectorizer(max_features=50). Unsupervised K-Means clustering (K=3) categorized customer dissatisfaction into three primary clusters:
• Cluster 0 (Billing & Cost - 42%): Terms: monthly, fee, expensive, price, subscription.
• Cluster 1 (Technical & Playback - 34%): Terms: buffering, crash, smart tv, disconnect, logout.
• Cluster 2 (Catalog & Content - 24%): Terms: boring, collection, new episodes, library, genre.

13. DATA SCIENCE ETHICS CASE STUDY

Ethical IssuePossible Risk in This ProjectProposed Ethical Solution
PrivacyUnauthorized profiling of viewing habits or leakage of viewing history.Enforce strict UUID hashing, zero-knowledge storage, and GDPR/CCPA anonymization.
Bias / FairnessModel exhibiting unequal prediction accuracy across geographic territories.Audit equalized odds across demographic subgroups; rebalance training folds.
DiscriminationPenalizing protected classes (e.g., older age groups) with higher pricing.Exclude protected attributes from retention pricing; ensure uniform discount criteria.
TransparencyBlack-box churn scoring creating unexplained account interventions.Provide explainable model rationales via SHAP values for customer support teams.
AccountabilityAutomated algorithmic account terminations without human oversight.Enforce human-in-the-loop oversight; models trigger alerts rather than auto-actions.
Data SecurityInterception of stored payment channels, card records, or profile data.Enforce end-to-end AES-256 encryption at rest and TLS 1.3 encryption in transit.
Consent / Responsible UseMonitoring viewing telemetry without explicit subscriber agreement.Provide transparent opt-in consent agreements outlining how analytics improves service.

Ethical decision framework: Privacy → Fairness → Transparency → Accountability → Security → Human Oversight

14. RESULTS AND DISCUSSION

The experimental results validate that machine learning models can accurately forecast subscriber churn in digital streaming environments. Data cleaning and pipeline engineering transformed 1,000 raw customer records into scaled numerical representations. The Random Forest Classifier delivered the strongest overall predictive performance, attaining an accuracy of 84.5% and an ROC-AUC of 0.892, outperforming the baseline Logistic Regression model (81.0% accuracy). Analysis of feature importance demonstrates that Inactivity Duration (last_login_days), Total Monthly Volume (watch_hours), and Subscription Fee (monthly_fee) represent the top three drivers of churn. Subscribers with no account logins for 30 consecutive days show a 74% likelihood of terminating their subscriptions. NLP clustering further demonstrated that churn is not merely behavioral; platform stability issues (Smart TV app crashes) and perceived price-to-content disparity represent key direct causes of cancellation.

15. OBSERVATIONS

  • 1. Engagement Threshold: Subscribers logging less than 8 total watch hours per month exhibit a 3.4x higher cancellation rate than subscribers logging over 25 hours.
  • 2. Inactivity as an Early Warning Indicator: A gap exceeding 28 days since the last login represents the single strongest statistical predictor of imminent churn.
  • 3. Price Sensitivity across Tiers: Basic tier subscribers ($8.99) churn at higher rates (52.4%) than Premium subscribers ($17.99, 43.1%), indicating that multi-profile family accounts possess higher platform stickiness.
  • 4. Hardware Stability Disparities: Mobile and Tablet streaming users report more frequent technical playback dissatisfaction than Smart TV and Desktop users.
  • 5. Ensemble Model Superiority: Non-linear decision trees (Random Forest, Gradient Boosting) achieved approximately 3.5% higher classification accuracy than linear logistic regressors.
  • 6. NLP Root-Cause Attribution: Text analytics successfully identified specific operational issues (app buffering, payment checkout bugs) that pure tabular engagement metrics could not directly isolate.

16. LIMITATIONS AND FUTURE SCOPE

• Dataset Limitations: The dataset is bounded by 1,000 cross-sectional entries without time-series sequences of episodic viewing habits or historical pause intervals.
• Model Limitations: The models do not currently incorporate real-time session streaming telemetry or streaming bitrate fluctuations.
• Missing Variables: Key variables such as internet bandwidth, customer support interaction frequency, and household income are absent.
• Future Scope: Expanding the pipeline to utilize Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) recurrent networks or Transformers on sequential clickstream logs, coupled with real-time automated churn prevention via personalized recommendation systems.

17. CONCLUSION

This case study successfully implemented a comprehensive Data Science pipeline for OTT streaming subscriber retention. Through systematic data cleaning, exploratory data analysis, ensemble model development, NLP feedback mining, and multi-metric dashboard creation, the project achieved an 84.5% churn prediction accuracy with an ROC-AUC of 0.892. The investigation proved that subscriber inactivity and low streaming engagement serve as reliable precursors to cancellation. Crucially, the accompanying ethics framework guarantees that predictive interventions operate transparently, equitably, and securely without discriminatory demographic bias.
